cds.title: University of Vermont Common Data Set 2025-2026 (PDF, Office of Institutional Research and Assessment)

stats.notes: From the Common Data Set (fall 2025 entering class; the PDF's page headers still read 'Common Data Set 2024-2025' but every figure is dated Fall 2025). Test-optional: 32% of enrolled first-year students submitted SAT scores (887) and 8% ACT (238); UVM's admissions pages say 45% of applicants submitted scores. UVM left the high-school GPA tables (C11/C12) blank in this CDS, so no average GPA or GPA distribution is stored; UVM's admissions page gives an admitted-student GPA of 3.5-3.8 (4.0 scale). The ED figure covers binding Early Decision (396 applied, 363 admitted); UVM also has non-binding Early Action. Residency rows sum to the totals.

cost.notes: First-year, full-time costs from the Common Data Set (G1 ticks '2026-27 costs not available, late May 2026', so these are 2025-26 figures): in-state tuition $16,938, non-resident tuition $46,655, required fees $3,058, on-campus housing $9,614 plus meal plan $5,040 (the CDS lists them separately; room and board shown = their sum, $14,654). Estimated expenses (residents): books $1,320, transportation $630, other $2,443 (other shown = transportation + other). UVM's international page gives a 2026-27 I-20 estimate for proof of funding: tuition and fees $50,713, living expenses $17,724, other expenses $10,575 (books, health insurance, personal), total $79,012. Per the CDS (H6), 119 undergraduate degree-seeking nonresidents received institutional non-need-based aid, average $39,655 (this exceeds the $30,000 maximum merit award on UVM's scholarship page; the CDS does not explain the difference).
